scope: Both minkes and Risso, plus species-specific skin and facial corrections throughout the last nine-species batch. Older archive species remain unchanged.
skinCorrections: Independent skin artwork replaces source-albedo pigment and shared Sei-derived markings. Separate body, fin and upper/lower fluke charts prevent paint leakage. Fine color and optical detail cover pale lower jaws and ventral surfaces.
headCorrections: Paired recessed eye apertures and skin lids; native source jaws are retained, with authored oral commissures on Risso; closed single odontocete or paired mysticete blowholes. Risso muzzle locally rounded.
pilotPectoral: Selected root-to-tip reconstruction near 23% of body length, checked against a published 18–27% range. This refers to pectoral flippers; at-sea identification can remain difficult.
limits: External artist reconstruction with generated skin detail, not a scan, color-calibrated photo projection, measured reflectance or fitted individual. Exact scratch patterns are illustrative. Physiology cards and mitochondrial data are evidence-linked reading; feeding, flow and tissue function are not computed.
movement: Existing authored posterior/fluke strokes, stable pectorals, banked turns, glide and selected Risso right spin-dive retained. Timing and trajectories are illustrative.

species.name: Pygmy right whale
species.changes: Smooth gray-to-pale ventral skin with no callosity pads or rorqual throat-pleat field. Recessed lateral eyes and skin-covered arched lip margins.

species.name: Sei whale
species.changes: Independent dark steel-gray skin with sparse pale healed oval scars, pale ventral epidermis, a single rostral ridge and a shorter ventral groove field.

species.name: Common minke whale
species.changes: Selected Northern Hemisphere common minke: dark upper body, subdued gray shoulder wash, pale underside and a midpectoral white band. Skin detail covers both jaws and belly; recessed lateral eyes and narrow closed lip crease.

species.name: Antarctic minke whale
species.changes: Selected Antarctic minke: independently authored gray flank lobes and pale ventral skin, dark pectorals without a northern-type transverse band, and a shorter selected throat-groove field.

species.name: Rice's whale
species.changes: Independent, relatively smooth dark-gray skin and pale underside; three rostral ridges and symmetric lower-jaw pigment. Shared source scars from the Sei mesh have been removed.

species.name: Bryde’s / Eden’s whale
species.changes: Separate coastal Eden/offshore Bryde display profiles retain three rostral ridges and symmetric jaw pigment. Each has a different authored skin map and individual scratch pattern. Color shade and scars do not diagnose the unresolved taxonomic forms.

species.name: Omura's whale
species.changes: Independent skin with pale right/dark left lower jaw, a right-side blaze, asymmetric chevrons and pale pectoral leading edges. Both lower jaws retain detailed skin; inner-gape anatomy is not claimed for this closed-mouth exterior.

species.name: Long-finned pilot whale
species.changes: Smooth charcoal-black skin, subdued saddle and ventral anchor marking replace painted glare. Swept pectorals extend toward a selected root-to-tip length near 23% of body length, within the published 18–27% range.

species.name: Risso's dolphin
species.changes: Selected mature Risso: a rounded beakless muzzle, median melon crease, recessed lateral eyes and short closed oral commissures. Fine gray epidermis and irregular pale rake-scar groups continue across the head and lower jaw; fins remain darker. Exact scars and pigment describe an illustrative individual.

checks.status: See release CI and delivered review images; tests check implementation invariants, not scientific certification.
